statements.text: Phenomenal transparency is the inaccessibility, for subjective experience, of the representational nature of the contents of experience. A transparent representation is not experienced as a representation, so the subject seems to be in direct contact with its content. It is a phenomenological notion, not an epistemological one, though it implies a lack of knowledge.

sources.quote: Transparency is a special form of darkness.
is a property of conscious representations, namely, that they are not experienced as representations
